Only the Qur\'an and the Sunnah that is sahih or hasan, upon the manhaj of the salaf. No duas or practices without evidence.

The base reference is Hisn al-Muslim, plus duas from the Qur\'an and authentic duas from the Sunnah that Hisn al-Muslim does not include. Each dua lists the book and hadith number, or the surah and ayah, which you can see by tapping the source label.

Grades are shown when stated in the takhrij of the source book, along with who graded them. Narrations graded weak by Shaykh al-Albani are not included. Duas from the Sunnah are only included when HadeethEnc.com grades them sahih or hasan.
Counts are shown only when stated in the Sunnah. No artificial targets, streaks, badges or worship statistics.

Only clear recitation, with no music, melodic intros or sound effects. The Hisn al-Muslim dhikr and dua audio is recited by Hamad ad-Duraihim, published by IslamHouse.com, and included unaltered. The duas from the Qur\'an are recited ayah by ayah by Sheikh Maher al-Muaiqly (Hafs), published by the King Fahd Glorious Qur\'an Printing Complex (qurancomplex.gov.sa) for free use in apps; the ayahs are joined in order, unaltered.

Duas and dhikr are taken from Hisn al-Muslim by Sa\'id bin Ali al-Qahtani: translation and takhrij from the Indonesian edition, Arabic text and English translation from hisnmuslim.com (IslamHouse.com), and for one entry the site misprints, from IslamHouse\'s English edition (Fortress of the Muslim, 2025). Narrations graded weak by al-Albani are not included. Duas from the Qur\'an are included as whole ayahs: Arabic text from Tanzil, translation by the Indonesian Ministry of Religious Affairs (Kementerian Agama RI) and, in English, Saheeh International, via QuranEnc.com. Duas from the Sunnah beyond Hisn al-Muslim come from HadeethEnc.com (Encyclopedia of Translated Prophetic Hadiths): Arabic text, grading, and Indonesian and English translations, included unaltered. The words of the dua are shown on top, and the whole hadith below. Each dua shows its source and takhrij.

The default calculation follows Kemenag RI, including its elevation correction for sunrise and Maghrib, and can be adjusted. Tested against Kemenag\'s official schedule for 16 cities across WIB, WITA and WIT: at most 1 minute apart. Imsak time is not shown.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_11_0
string-array.item: In the long opening dua of the night prayer, the recording leaves out two parts the book has. They now show muted with a dotted underline and are not highlighted during playback; the text stays as the book gives it.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_10_3
string-array.item: Two more recordings were re-timed: the dua against Satan\'s whispers now starts after the reciter\'s chapter title, and a waking-up dua\'s phrases light up in time with the recitation.
Two travel duas now also list their second source, al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim (no. 1883).

string-array.name: whats_new_1_10_2
string-array.item: The audio of 86 duas was checked word by word and now starts on the dua: the reciter\'s chapter title and read-aloud count notes are no longer played, and phrases light up in time with the recitation.
In the dhikr taught to the Bedouin (tasbih), the narration between its two parts is skipped.
Ten duas now show their hadith number, for example in al-Mustadrak, Musnad Ahmad and as-Sunan al-Kubra.
In routine recall, «Did you know it without the text?» sits below the Arabic, and its buttons stack at large text sizes.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_10_1
string-array.item: On Android 8–11, the widget now shows before a location is set and when it carries the «moved to Adwam» notice, instead of «Problem loading widget».

string-array.name: whats_new_1_10_0
string-array.item: Every dua now holds only the words to recite. The book\'s narration, instructions and count notes are under «See the full text in the book», and the translation is of the dua alone.
Entries with several sayings are split: each has its own count and audio, for example the istighfar and «Allahumma antas-salam» after prayer.
Virtue hadiths and instructions show as reading cards, without counter, memorisation or routines.
The audio of 156 duas now plays only the dua, and 104 duas have phrases that follow the recitation.
Evening dhikr that the book gives in the morning wording now show the evening wording as a note from the book.
Five duas show Darussalam\'s grading under «Other gradings». The widget no longer appears twice on Android 8–11, and the city list can be searched as soon as it opens.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_9_0
string-array.item: Memorise: Listen and Build now show one phrase at a time, following the audio, with Back and Next. Check still shows the whole text.
When you practise only the words you missed, the reveal button and first letters are there, even if none of the recital was right.
At large text sizes, Back and Next no longer break, and Next always stays on the right.
Morning and evening dhikr no. 13 no longer end with the word «or» (أَوْ) left over from the book\'s note, and the audio stops where the dhikr ends.
Hadith numbers added to 42 duas, and leftover marks from the book\'s PDF removed from seven duas\' Indonesian translation.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_8_0
string-array.item: The Aa button on a dua opens the reading display settings: layout, phrase colour, translation and text size. Changes show on the dua right away.
Choose how a dua is laid out: one phrase per line, flowing text as in the book with pause marks, or one phrase at a time with Back and Next.
Phrase colour: give each phrase an alternating or bubble background so you can see where it ends. While the audio plays, only the phrase being recited is coloured.
Memorise: in the Check step, tap the words you missed. The app suggests a rating, and you can practise just those words.
Eight morning, evening and sleep duas no longer sit inside the book\'s ((…)) marks. The book\'s notes after them stay, shown muted.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_7_0
string-array.item: Duas now show one phrase per line, so you can see where to pause and where to continue. Tap a phrase to play the recitation from there.
The book\'s notes in brackets, such as when to say a dua or how many times, now appear smaller and dimmer so they don\'t read as part of the dua.
Six duas from Hisn al-Muslim now hold only the words you recite, so their Latin transliteration shows too. The full text from the book is still below the dua.
Without a location, the Today screen still shows the morning and evening adhkar and your routines.
When you first open the app, you can choose your city yourself and set the size of the Arabic and the translation.
Search puts the occasion\'s name and the transliteration first, and now finds source books such as Bukhari.
If audio fails to play, the app now tells you.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_6_0
string-array.item: A new category, Duas from the Sunnah: 16 sahih and hasan duas that are not in Hisn al-Muslim, such as Yā muqallibal-qulūb, the dua for setting right one\'s religion, world and Hereafter, and seeking refuge from the loss of blessings. They come from HadeethEnc.com, with the whole hadith under each dua.
The full text from the source now also shows in English when you choose the English translation.
Tidier Latin transliteration: the name of Allah written without its shadda now reads, min before al- reads minal-, and the ends of phrases take their pausal form.
Memorization: tap Done reciting after reciting without looking. If you revealed no word, the hints fade one stage on their own; if you revealed many, a hint comes back.
When running a routine, a dua you recite from memory now counts as a review when it is due.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_5_0
string-array.item: The Duas page now has two tabs: My duas for your routines and All duas for the full library. Categories open in place, and routine cards show their first three duas.
Save a dua to your routines straight from its card, and tap Memorize to add it to My hifz.
Customize is replaced by routines: duas you had customized are now routines named after their occasion. In Settings, Backup and my sets is now just Backup.
Feedback and diagnostics now records when the prayer-times widget last refreshed, to help us fix a countdown that falls behind on some phones.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_4_2
string-array.item: 21 duas, among them the dhikr of ruku, sujud, the morning and evening adhkar and the dua for entering the masjid, now show only the words to recite. The book\'s full narration stays below them.
42 more duas are now split into phrases: the Build step, the A–B loop and highlighting of the phrase being recited now work for them.
Every Hisnul Muslim dua now has an English translation.
Latin transliteration fixes: where the source leaves out a vowel mark, no transliteration is shown rather than a guess.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_4_1
string-array.item: Latin transliteration is now available for most duas, generated from the Arabic text following the Indonesian (Kemenag–Kemendikbud) standard. Turn it on in Settings → Display.
33 duas, Sayyidul Istighfar among them, are now split into phrases: the Build step, the A–B loop and highlighting of the phrase being recited now work for them.
The Arabic of each dua now appears without the book\'s (( )) quotation marks.
Fixes for TalkBack users in the Recall step and on the dua page.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_4_0
string-array.item: English translations are now available for the Hisnul Muslim duas, from hisnmuslim.com (IslamHouse.com). Choose the language in Settings → Display.
The 31 duas from the Qur\'an can now be listened to, recited ayah by ayah by Sheikh Maher al-Muaiqly.
Duas with the same text, such as the morning and evening adhkar, are now memorized once. If you had saved both, the one you reviewed last is kept.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_3_1
string-array.item: In the Recall step, the Arabic now comes right after the cue, before the hiding options.
Memorize now shows where a dua sits in its set, e.g. \"Morning adhkar · 3 of 19\".

string-array.name: whats_new_1_3_0
string-array.item: While reading your adhkar, save a dua to memorize with \"Add to My hifz\" in the menu. It joins My hifz as \"Not started\" for later. You can also remove a dua from My hifz.
Add a dua to a routine straight from its page, and pick duas for a routine by their Arabic and translation.
The widget now has a see-through grey background and a neater \"PM\". Set its opacity in Settings → Display.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_2_0
string-array.item: Reviewing a memorized dua now starts from memory: the Arabic is covered, with a cue of when it is said and, if you need it, its meaning. Then check the full text and rate how it went.
In the Recall step, turn on \"Show first letters\" so each hidden word shows its first letter, hide words from the end of the dua, and tap \"Show the next word\" when you get stuck.
When reading your adhkar, a dua you are memorizing appears without its Arabic so you can recite it from memory. Tap \"Show the text\" to check; you can turn this off in the menu.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_1_0
string-array.item: The prayer-times widget has a new look: the large figure is now the current time, and under it the time left until the next prayer, with that prayer\'s time, such as \"2 hr 47 min until Maghrib 5:51 PM\".
Its background is now translucent black glass, with the sun by day and the moon at that night\'s phase, drawn from NASA imagery.
Prayer names show above their times along the bottom of the widget, and the Hijri date is now written like the regular date.

string-array.name: whats_new_1_0_1
string-array.item: The prayer-times widget no longer has a thick border: its card now fills nearly the whole widget.
On taller 4×2 widgets, such as on Samsung phones, the prayer names now show above their times, along with the line below, such as "Dhuha until 11:30".

string-array.name: whats_new_1_0_0
string-array.item: Adwam now installs as a new app. The first time you open it, your data moves over from the old one; then allow notifications again and add the widget again.
The prayer-times widget has a new look: the next prayer and its time stand out, the time left reads in hours and minutes, and a bar shows how far the day has gone.
On first install the app now always opens in Indonesian, even when your phone is in English.
The Wear OS tile has been removed. If you used it, the tile on your watch no longer updates and you can remove it from the watch.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_9_0
string-array.item: On phones that have it, the prayer-times widget now uses Google Sans, closer to the app\'s look.
Getting ready for the next Adwam, which will install as a new app: your data will be able to move straight over.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_8_1
string-array.item: Easier to use with TalkBack: buttons and checklist items are read clearly, including the ones not done yet, and focus no longer jumps back to the top.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_8_0
string-array.item: Muslim Daily is now called Adwam (أدوم), meaning “the most constant”. Your content, notes, memorization and settings stay as they are.
A new icon on your home screen, in notifications and on Wear OS. On Android 13 and later it follows your phone’s themed icons.
If the prayer-times widget is slow to move to the next prayer, Today now shows a note to allow exact alarms.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_0_final
string-array.item: A more compact Today screen: a shorter next-prayer card, with Qibla and Nearby masjid right below the time.
Morning and evening adhkar, prohibited times and Dhuha now appear only while their time is running.
Open Fajr or Isha to see when its time ends. Witr is now ticked inside Isha.
Also in 0.7: a new prayer-times widget for every size, and a faster, lighter app.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_0_beta_4
string-array.item: The app now opens faster and is lighter: the download is about a third smaller, and scrolling feels smoother.
The widget uses less memory, with the same look.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_0_beta_3
string-array.item: A tidier, easier-to-read widget: the same spacing at every size, with the next prayer always the most prominent.
On a tall widget the times now sit in two rows with larger type, instead of leaving empty space.
A one-column widget shows more of the coming prayers, neatly from the top.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_0_beta_2
string-array.item: Times in the widget are no longer cut off at any size, also in English and with the 12-hour clock.
On a tall, wide widget the next prayer now shows large, and the times in the row are bigger.
The widget\'s countdown stays right after you resize it, and its corners are round on Android 8–11.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_0
string-array.item: One prayer-times widget for every size, from 1×1 to 5×3. The bigger it is, the more it shows: the Hijri date, the place, today\'s times and a sunnah fast tomorrow.
The widget\'s sky is more realistic and follows the prayer times, in the same typeface as the app.
After Isya the widget shows tomorrow\'s times. Widgets you already placed switch to the new look.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_6_0
string-array.item: My note: write a private note on any dua. It stays on your device and in your backups.
Join the beta: in Settings → Updates, turn on beta to get new versions early.
This screen appears once after each update.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_5_3
string-array.item: Choose the Arabic typeface in Display and text. The default is now Noto Naskh Arabic, clearer on phone screens.
The audio player and Start reading now sit neatly on top of the bottom menu.
One Adjust button to choose and reorder duas.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_5_2
string-array.item: My routines: pick duas from anywhere, order them, and read them one after another like the morning adhkar.
Theme colours now fill the width of the screen.
